title: Buffered retries and graceful stream degradation for SDK clients
creator: Anika Patel
description: Add a consistent client-side pattern across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that combines small in-memory buffering, idempotent retry envelopes, and graceful degradation modes for streaming responses. Goal: reduce surface area of user-visible errors for transient infra problems while keeping predictable latency and clear developer-facing recovery guidance.
motivation: Customers report brittle streaming behavior when an upstream token-exhaustion or transient GPU OOM occurs: SDKs either fail the entire stream or retry in a way that confuses application logic. We need a unified approach that preserves partial progress, gives actionable error messages, and offers deterministic fallbacks (resume, partial-result envelope, or switch to request/response).
proposal: Implement a client-side "buffered retry" layer that:
proposal_points: 1) Buffering: Maintain a small soft buffer (configurable, default 4KB / 1 message) of the latest outgoing request chunk(s) and associated KV cache cursor/resume token so we can safely retry only the minimal window on retryable failures.

2) Idempotent envelopes: Attach an idempotency key + sequence offset for multi-chunk streams so server-side dedup/resume can be used when available. Enforce conservative defaults when server doesn't support resume (fall back to application-visible partial results).

3) Retry policy: Exponential backoff with jitter, capped retries (default 3), and backpressure detection (if repeated 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED escalate to graceful degradation), plus per-language ergonomic defaults and overrides.

4) Graceful degradation modes: three modes - fail-fast (existing behavior), partial-result (complete with a "partial": true envelope and a resume_token when available), and request/response fallback (switch to a non-streaming API path automatically).

5) Developer guidance: Standardized error codes and human-friendly messages across SDKs: RETRYABLE_TRANSIENT, NONRETRYABLE_FINAL, PARTIAL_COMPLETE_WITH_RESUME, FALLBACK_TO_POLLING. Each error includes: code, user_message, retry_after (ms), resume_token (when present), and diagnostic_id (trace link).
technical_design: The SDK-level adapter lives between the network transport and the public streaming iterator/callback. It tracks minimal state: seq_offset, last_acknowledged_cursor, last_sent_chunk_hash. On a retryable transport error, it applies a deterministic rewind to seq_offset and republishes only buffered chunks. Languages will share the same wire semantics (headers: X-Redwood-Idempotency, X-Redwood-Seq-Offset, X-Redwood-Resume-Token) and the same canonical error envelope JSON for non-stream termination messages.
language_ergonomics: Python: async iterator wrapper that yields the same StreamingChunk objects. Retry loop lives in _BufferedStreamClient. Provides 'resume_token' attribute on StreamResult and raises a RestartableStreamError with .resume_token when relevant.
TypeScript: ReadableStream wrapper + AsyncIterable. Exposes 'onResume' callback and a StreamFailure error class matching the Python fields. Default behavior mirrors Python (partial-result mode).
Go: io.Reader-like stream with ResumeToken() on the returned StreamResult. Error types implement errors.Is for RETRYABLE_TRANSIENT and include a DiagnosticID().
acceptance_criteria: Automated integration tests (Python/TS/Go) covering: success path, single transient failure with successful retry (buffer replayed), repeated transient failures reaching graceful partial-result, resume flow when server supports resume-token, and fallback to polling mode.
SDK exposes config knobs: buffer_size_bytes, max_retries, retry_backoff_ms_base, degradation_mode (fail_fast|partial|fallback), and telemetry hooks.
Error envelopes conform to agreed spec and map to SDK error classes in each language. Example messages present in user docs.
E2E perf regression <= 5% median latency on cold streaming compared to current SDKs when retries are disabled.
Design/PRD reviewed by SDK lead (Eva Chen), Runtime lead (Mateo Ruiz), and Security for headers/consent (SAML/KMS implications considered).
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and SDK config default 'degradation_mode=partial' opt-in for two-week canary. Steps: 1) Merge server resume-token support (runtime rollout) 2) Release SDK beta with feature flag off 3) Enable feature for 10% of hosted traffic with automatic telemetry 4) Gradually increase to 100% if error rates drop and no regressions found.
open_decisions: Should default degradation_mode be 'partial' or 'fail_fast'? PM prefers 'partial' for UX; infra is concerned about telemetry inflation. Decided to canary with 'partial'.
How large should default buffer_size_bytes be? Proposal: 4KB (tunable).
Do we include automatic disk-backed buffering for low-memory clients? MVP = in-memory only.
implementation_notes: Server changes: optional support for resume tokens in stream close envelope and idempotent deduping keyed by X-Redwood-Idempotency + seq. SDK changes: thin common spec, then language-specific wrappers with shared test vectors. Add telemetry events: stream_retry_attempt, stream_degraded, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Buffered replay could resend user-sensitive chunks. Mitigation: Do not buffer chunks flagged as 'sensitive' by API; default redact and mark as non-replayable. Add explicit opt-in for replayable_streams.
Risk: Resume semantics inconsistent across server versions. Mitigation: SDK negotiates resume capability at stream open and falls back to partial/fail_fast modes.
Risk: Complex API surface across languages. Mitigation: Keep public surface minimal and provide ergonomic helpers in each SDK.
Risk: Telemetry noise. Mitigation: emit aggregated counters and sample full traces.
Risk: Security headers interaction. Mitigation: Security review confirmed no KMS impact; idempotency headers carry no secrets.

example_snippets:
Python async iterator usage example:

from redwood import StreamingClient, DegradationMode

client = StreamingClient(degradation_mode=DegradationMode.PARTIAL, buffer_size_bytes=4096, max_retries=3)

async for chunk in client.stream_generate(prompt):
    if chunk.partial:
        print('Partial result available; resume_token:', chunk.resume_token)
    print(chunk.text)
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapter logic + shared test vectors across languages. Integration harness simulating transient errors (TCP resets, 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, OOM close) to validate buffered replay and resume_token behavior. Run a 48h canary with 10% traffic routing and automated rollback thresholds (error_rate > 2x baseline for 30m).
